criterion_notes.c1: Examines gaining and losing household/individual access to piped water (at least one private or shared compound tap in the dwelling, plot, or yard) in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording: Yes — examines housing/property tenure status (owner/co-owner, renting/co-renting, parents' or other's residence), formal urban land-zoning status (downtown, zoned periphery, non-zoned periphery), formal vs. informal sector employment, and policy periods across ONEA's institutional regimes (1985 'shared water management' prioritizing public standpipes; 1994 restructuring into a state-owned company governed by private law). Narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: Yes (borderline) — although 75% of gains and 97% of losses occur via residential moves rather than in-situ connection changes, 25% of gains are in-dwelling new connections and 3% of losses are disconnections mostly for non-payment of water bills, and the Cox models directly estimate the effects and interaction of housing tenure status (Residence status) and formal land-zoning status (Zone of residence), where the authors explicitly note that connection to the ONEA piped network is not permitted/possible in non-zoned areas held via customary plot purchase from traditional chiefs prior to formal municipal zoning and plot allocation. Tenure status and formal land-zoning/tenure eligibility rules governing network connection fall within the rule-type mechanism scope.
criterion_notes.c3: Quantitative empirical study applying Kaplan-Meier survival curves and semi-parametric Cox proportional hazard models to retrospective life-history survey data from the 2000 nationally representative EMIUB survey in Burkina Faso.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports instantaneous hazard ratios and survival probabilities for two service-access transitions: (1) first transition from living in a residence without piped water to one with piped water, and (2) first loss of piped water access (via moving or in-dwelling disconnection for bill non-payment).
criterion_notes.c5: Unit of analysis is the individual observed across residential spells from age 15 (or arrival in Ouagadougou after age 15). Population, sample sizes (2,839 respondents in Ouagadougou plus 294 former residents; risk sets of 2,134 for first access and 1,226 [1,220 in text] for first loss), time-varying tenure and zoning exposures, piped-water transition outcomes, and retrospective event-history survey design are all clearly specified.

raw_response.exposure: Time-varying housing tenure status (owner/co-owner, renting/co-renting, parents' residence, other's residence), formal urban zoning status of zone of residence (downtown, zoned periphery, non-zoned customary-tenure periphery where piped water connections are not possible), and their interaction, alongside historical policy periods (before 1970, 1970-79, 1980-89, 1990-2000), formal vs. informal employment, education, marital status, migration origin, and sex.
raw_response.outcome: Instantaneous probability (hazard) and waiting time of (1) first gaining access to piped water (at least one tap in the dwelling, plot, or yard) and (2) first losing access to piped water (through residential move or utility disconnection for non-payment).
raw_response.population_and_sample: Men and women aged 15-64 from the 2000 nationally representative EMIUB retrospective survey in Burkina Faso who lived in Ouagadougou after age 15 (2,839 interviewed in Ouagadougou and 294 former residents interviewed elsewhere; analytical risk sets of n = 2,134 individuals for first access and n = 1,226 [reported as 1,220 in text] for first loss of piped water).
raw_response.rationale: This empirical event-history study analyzes gaining and losing on-plot/in-dwelling piped water access in Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso using nationally representative retrospective life-history survey data (EMIUB 2000). It satisfies all inclusion criteria under both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2: Cox proportional hazard models directly estimate the main and interactive effects of housing tenure status (owner/co-owner vs. tenant/co-renter vs. hosted) and formal urban land-zoning status (downtown, zoned periphery, and non-zoned periphery where plots are bought from customary chiefs prior to formal municipal zoning/allocation and where ONEA piped water connections are not permitted/possible), while also documenting in-dwelling new connections (25% of gains) and disconnections for bill non-payment (3% of losses). Confidence is medium rather than high because most observed transitions occur via residential mobility across housing/zoning strata rather than direct administrative screening of connection applications.
raw_response.study_design: Retrospective cohort / event-history analysis (Kaplan-Meier survival curves and semi-parametric Cox proportional hazard models) using a two-stage stratified probability survey (EMIUB 2000).
